passage:
Tuesday: Devika opened the app for one quick look at a cooking clip. Ninety minutes later she was still there, watching strangers shout at each other, each video angrier than the last, her jaw tight. Her homework sat untouched.
Friday: Manjula noticed her friend's puffy eyes. "You keep saying the app knows what you like. I think it knows what keeps you." Devika frowned, then admitted that whenever she paused on an upsetting clip, more of them came.
The next Wednesday: Devika set a daily limit, unfollowed the angry pages and followed two pottery makers. When the reminder buzzed, she put the phone in a drawer and helped her mother chop onions.

qa.q: What did Devika follow after she unfollowed the angry pages?
What was Devika feeling as the clips got angrier, and what tells you?
qa.a: She was getting tense and upset, shown by her tight jaw, yet she kept watching because each clip pulled her to the next.

qa.q: Why do Devika's steps suit an app built to hold attention?
qa.a: Setting a daily limit, curating what she follows and stepping away when the reminder buzzed all cut down how much the feed can keep serving her.

qa.q: How might Manjula have seen the change in Devika?
qa.a: Manjula noticed the puffy eyes and explained gently, so probably felt worried at first and relieved to see Devika take control.

grounding: Shows a teen recognising a feed designed for attention and setting limits and curating follows.

passage:
Karthik had opened the app at eight to check one video about the cricket match. When he looked up, it was 11:20.

He'd watched a clip of two men shouting on a news debate, then another, then an angrier one. Then videos of road rage. Then a man ranting about his school board. His jaw was clenched and his head ached. He couldn't remember one useful thing he'd seen.

His sister Anjali, passing his door, said, "You've been on that since dinner."

"I don't even like these videos," he said, surprised by his own voice. "They just keep coming."

"Because you keep watching. The app learns what keeps you there. Anger works."

Karthik thought about that. The next day he set a forty-five minute limit on the app. He tapped "not interested" on every shouting video and followed three cricket analysis channels and a cooking one. After his limit ended, he went down to the colony ground.

The feed looked different by Sunday. Calmer. So did he.

qa.q: What time was it when Karthik looked up from the app?
What was Karthik feeling after hours of the angry videos?
qa.a: Karthik felt tense and drained, with a clenched jaw and an aching head, and surprised that he had kept watching.

qa.q: What changes did Karthik make, and why do they help?
qa.a: Karthik set a forty-five minute limit, marked shouting videos as not interested and followed calmer channels, which weakens the app's hold on his attention.

qa.q: How does Anjali see what the app is doing to Karthik?
qa.a: Anjali sees the app as designed to keep him watching, using anger to hold his attention.

grounding: It shows a teen whose feed keeps serving upsetting content until hours vanish, recognising that the app is designed for attention and setting limits, curating follows and stepping away.

passage:
"Gautam, you're still up?" Bhavna whispered from the doorway. The glow of his phone lit his face.

"Can't sleep."

"What are you watching?"

"Videos about exam failures. People who flopped their boards and ruined their lives." His voice was flat. "It keeps showing me more."

Bhavna sat on the edge of his bed. "Why are you watching that two weeks before your exams?"

"I watched one. Now it's all it gives me."

"That's how it works. It noticed you stopped on one, so now it's feeding you fear because you keep watching." She took the phone gently. "Here. Long-press. 'Not interested.' And this one. And this one."

"That's it?"

"No. Follow some study channels you actually like. And set a timer: one hour a day. Then put it on the charger in the hall."

Gautam let out a breath. "I feel sick from all that."

"I know. Tomorrow, walk with me in the morning instead."

qa.q: What kind of videos was Gautam watching?
qa.a: Gautam was watching videos about exam failures.

qa.q: What was Gautam feeling after watching the exam-failure videos?
qa.a: Gautam felt anxious and sick, flat and unable to sleep two weeks before his exams.

qa.q: What steps did Bhavna suggest, and why are they wise?
qa.a: Bhavna suggested marking videos as not interested, following useful study channels, a one-hour timer and charging the phone outside, which breaks the feed's fear loop.

qa.q: How does Bhavna see the app's effect on Gautam?
qa.a: Bhavna sees the app feeding him fear because he keeps watching, and wants to protect him before his exams.

grounding: It shows a teen whose feed serves more of what upsets him until hours vanish, recognising the app's design and setting limits, curating follows and stepping away.
